page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-80 is a high-capacity general-purpose virtual machine built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 80 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 40 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, powered by Intel Xeon processors. The instance configuration includes 320 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction flags include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI vector extensions. The instance features no bundled local storage and includes zero GPUs, requiring network-attached persistent storage for data persistence.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-threaded computational capabilities and high memory bandwidth. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 75092.52, while PassMark registered a CPU score of 52649.44 and an extended instructions score of 65354.92. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth reached 213.45 GB/sec for reads and 94.1 GB/sec for writes. Real-world workload tests highlight strong performance across concurrent operations, including 63.15 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, 41350.0 in Geekbench Clang software compilation, and 22522.26 in PassMark database operations. In contrast, single-thread metrics remain in the middle 50% tier, and large-model text generation falls to bottom-tier throughput due to the absence of dedicated hardware accelerators.

Regarding resource efficiency, the n2-standard-80 delivers high physical core density and strong multi-core scalability without the overhead of fractional scheduling. The balanced allocation of compute and memory makes it well suited for large enterprise relational databases, in-memory Redis caches, high-concurrency continuous integration pipelines, and heavy web service backends. Workloads with heavy I/O requirements must account for external storage attachments, while machine learning inference on large parameter models is constrained by the CPU-only profile.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-80 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 80 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs across 40 physical cores at 2.8 GHz, paired with 320 GB of system memory. Lacking integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on network storage while providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Benchmark results show strong multi-core computational throughput, sustained high memory bandwidth, and strong performance in Redis operations, Clang compilation, and database transactions. Single-core performance remains average, and LLM text generation on large models is limited due to the absence of hardware accelerators. Given its dense compute capacity and memory allocation, the n2-standard-80 is designed for large-scale enterprise databases, distributed in-memory caching clusters, continuous integration build environments, and containerized backend workloads.
